model_output.verdict: Accounts payable work in Houston, backed by senior accounting experience, with a few responsibilities still needing detail.
write_up: You process around 400 vendor invoices a month in QuickBooks and have earlier experience with financial statements, an audit and a small accounting team. A recruiter can see the fit for accounts payable or staff accounting, though your part in the current month-end close is still a question.

The strongest line is the one about reducing month-end closing from 12 days to 7 days. It names what you made and shows the change in closing time. Use that level of detail to explain the work you helped with and what your team handled.

cards.line: - Help the controller for month end closing
cards.cannot_tell: 'Help' hides your part of the close. A recruiter can't tell which accounts or tasks you handled alongside the controller.
cards.example: Help the controller with month end closing by completing [tasks]
cards.question: Which month-end closing tasks did you handle for the controller?

cards.cannot_tell: The team count is there, but not the work. What did the junior accountants handle under your direction?
cards.example: Lead team of 3 junior accountants who handle [work the team handles]
cards.question: What work did the 3 junior accountants handle?

cards.line: - Reduce the month end closing from 12 days to 7 days by make new checklist and template
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as your model. The checklist and template give the shorter close a concrete story.

fit.note: Your current invoice and payment work points toward accounts payable, while your earlier general ledger and financial statement work supports a staff accountant search. The US GAAP certificate adds useful context; the resume doesn't say how you've applied US GAAP on the job.
